Summary and SLOOS overlay:
- Policy: The FOMC held the funds rate at 5.25–5.50% and signaled no cuts until there’s “greater confidence” inflation is moving to 2%. QT was modestly tapered by lowering the Treasury runoff cap to $25b (from $60b), with the MBS cap unchanged at $35b and excess MBS principal reinvested into Treasuries—leaving overall policy restrictive.
- SLOOS signals tighter credit supply and softer demand: Banks reported tighter standards and wider spreads for C&I loans, weaker C&I loan demand, and higher borrower-quality requirements (e.g., credit scores). CRE lending standards tightened further, including wider spreads, lower LTVs, higher DSCRs, shorter interest-only periods, and reduced market areas, with banks citing economic outlook, reduced risk tolerance, and property-market fundamentals (rents, vacancies, prices). Consumer credit (credit cards, autos, other) also saw tighter terms and credit limits, with higher loan rates and stricter terms for riskier segments.
- Interpretation: SLOOS indicates financial conditions are already restrictive and likely to weigh on credit creation and growth, which complements the FOMC’s cautious stance and reduces the urgency to hike again. The QT taper marginally eases term premia, but the credit-channel tightening from banks keeps overall conditions tight. This tilts the tone slightly away from hawkishness on the margin, even as sticky inflation keeps cuts contingent on renewed progress.

Net tone: balanced but cautious; hawkish on inflation, tempered by SLOOS-evident credit tightening. Adjusted slightly below neutral.
